title: SELF-INSTRUCT: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
data_curation: This is the paper's core contribution: synthesizing instruction data from the model itself. It seeds the pipeline with 175 human-written tasks (25 classification, 150 non-classification, authored without reference to existing datasets). The four-step pipeline: (1) Instruction Generation samples 8 in-context examples (6 human + 2 model-generated) to prompt new task instructions; (2) Classification Task Identification uses few-shot prompting (12 clf + 19 non-clf seeds); (3) Instance Generation uses an input-first approach for non-classification tasks and an output-first approach for classification (generate class labels first, then condition each input on a label to avoid label bias); (4) Filtering rejects instructions with ROUGE-L > 0.7 to any existing one, drops image/picture/graph keywords, removes duplicate/same-input-different-output instances, and applies length/repetition heuristics. Output: 52,445 instructions (11,584 clf, 40,861 non-clf) and 82,439 instances (35,878 with empty input). Expert quality audit on 200 samples: 92% valid task, 79% appropriate input, 58% correct output, 54% all-fields-valid. Generation cost ~$600; the dataset is publicly released.
curriculum: Not a multi-stage training curriculum. The pipeline is a single supervised finetuning stage: generate synthetic instruction data, then finetune the SAME model (GPT3 davinci, 175B) that produced the data. Finetuning runs through OpenAI's API with default hyperparameters, prompt_loss_weight set to 0, and 2 epochs to avoid overfitting; multiple prompt templates (varied Task:/Input:/Output: prefixes and line breaks) encode each example for format robustness. The bootstrapping loop is over data, not training stages. A scaling ablation shows gains plateau after ~16K instructions on user-oriented eval (and earlier, at hundreds, on SUPERNI). An optional second step regenerates outputs with InstructGPT003 (distillation) and yields ~+10% on user-oriented eval, hinting at a quality-refinement stage, but this is presented as future work rather than the core recipe.
method: SELF-INSTRUCT is a semi-automated, almost annotation-free framework for instruction tuning using a pretrained LM's own generations. The core algorithm is an iterative bootstrapping loop over a task pool: seed tasks -> generate new instructions (in-context prompted) -> classify each as classification/non-classification -> generate input-output instances -> filter -> add survivors back to the pool -> repeat. The key algorithmic trick is the output-first instance generation for classification tasks: it first emits class labels, then conditions input generation on each label, counteracting the bias where a naive input-first approach over-produces one label (e.g., mostly grammatical inputs for grammar-error detection). Filtering combines ROUGE-L<0.7 de-duplication, keyword exclusion, and heuristic validity checks. The authors frame it as a form of self-distillation where source and target are the same model and the distilled content is instruction tasks. It targets the limited quantity, diversity, and creativity of human-written instruction data (PROMPTSOURCE/SUPERNI skew toward popular NLP tasks). Training itself is standard supervised SFT.
eval_metrics: Two evaluations. (1) SUPERNI benchmark (119 tasks x 100 instances, zero-shot, ROUGE-L): GPT3SELF-INST scores 39.9 vs vanilla GPT3 6.8 (+33.1 absolute), T0 33.1, GPT3+T0-training 37.9, InstructGPT001 40.8; with SUPERNI training added, GPT3SELF-INST+SUPER NI reaches 51.6 (best). (2) A newly curated set of 252 user-oriented novel instructions judged by expert authors on a 4-level scale (A valid / B acceptable minor errors / C significant errors / D invalid), with inter-rater Cohen's kappa 0.57-0.58 (4-class), 0.75 (binary A/B vs C/D), and Spearman rho 0.81; counting A+B as valid, GPT3SELF-INST beats T0- and SUPERNI-trained GPT3 baselines by a large margin and trails InstructGPT001 by only ~5%. Baselines span T5-LM (11B), GPT3 (175B), T0/Tk-INSTRUCT (11B), and InstructGPT001/002/003. Data-size and distillation-quality ablations are also reported.
key_results: GPT3SELF-INST (GPT3 175B finetuned on 52K self-generated instructions) improves over vanilla GPT3 by +33.1 absolute ROUGE-L on SUPERNI (39.9 vs 6.8), nearly matching InstructGPT001 (40.8). On 252 user-oriented instructions it beats public-dataset-tuned baselines by a large margin and lands only ~5% behind InstructGPT001. Distilling the outputs via InstructGPT003 adds ~+10% on the user-oriented eval.
evolution_note: Building on the 2022 instruction-tuning wave (T0, SUPERNI/FLAN, InstructGPT) and LM-based data generation, SELF-INSTRUCT reacts against the human-annotation cost and opacity of commercial instruction-tuned models, pioneering self-bootstrapped synthetic instruction data that directly enables later open self-instruct-style models (Alpaca, Baize) and motivates distillation/reward-based refinement of synthetic instruction corpora.
